chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who has a share of water (shirb) with a group of people in a canal, wherein there are partners. If some of them become self-sufficient from their share, can he sell his share? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, if he wishes, he can sell it for silver (dirhams), and if he wishes, he can sell it for a measure of wheat.'

key_terms.الشِّرْبُ: Share of water or right to draw water from a source

ai.seo_question: Can a partner sell their share of water in a shared canal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of transferring water rights (shirb) within a shared irrigation system, affirming that the owner retains full autonomy to sell their share regardless of the partners' needs. It highlights the flexibility in valuation, allowing payment in either silver currency or wheat, which reflects the practical economic realities of agrarian societies in early Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that water shares are treated as distinct, tradable assets rather than fixed communal obligations.
